findings.title: Record separator injection in git log parser bypasses credit/authorship policy enforcement
findings.attack_path:
Attacker: any contributor who can push commits to a repository where creditlint runs in CI or audit mode.

Controlled input: the commit message body. Git permits arbitrary bytes in commit messages, including the 0x1e (Record Separator) control character.

Path to vulnerable code: creditlint's `audit --all` and `check --range` commands invoke `git log --format=%H%x1f%an%x1f%ae%x1f%cn%x1f%ce%x1f%B%x1e` (collect_all_messages / collect_range_messages in src/git.rs). The `%B` placeholder emits the raw commit message body verbatim, so a 0x1e byte embedded in the message is written to the output stream indistinguishably from the intended record terminator. parse_git_log_stream splits the stream on 0x1e, producing a first record with the real metadata and a truncated message, and a second 'record' containing the remainder of the message (e.g. the forbidden trailer line). parse_git_log_records then calls splitn(6, 0x1f) on each record; the second record has only one field, so the second `fields.next()?` returns None and filter_map silently discards it. The forbidden trailer is never passed to policy.analyze.

Proof of concept: a commit with message 'legit subject\x1e\nCo-authored-by: Codex <codex@example.com>' passes `creditlint audit --all` with exit code 0 and zero violations, while the same trailer without the 0x1e byte is correctly flagged with exit code 1.
findings.impact: The core security function of the tool—detecting unauthorized authorship and credit metadata—is completely bypassed for any commit whose message contains a 0x1e byte before the forbidden content. An attacker can hide AI/tool authorship markers (Co-authored-by, Made-with, Generated-with, etc.) from CI audit checks and range-based policy scans, defeating compliance enforcement. The commit-msg hook path (--message-file/--stdin) is unaffected, so the bypass specifically targets the CI/audit workflows that are the primary deployment model described in the project README and AGENTS.md.
findings.remediation: Use a delimiter that cannot appear in git commit content. Git commit messages cannot contain NUL (0x00) bytes, so switch the record and field separators to NUL-terminated format: use `git log -z --format=%H%x00%an%x00%ae%x00%cn%x00%ce%x00%B` and split on 0x00 in the parser. Alternatively, fetch each commit's message individually via `git show -s --format=%B <sha>` to avoid any delimiter collision. As defense-in-depth, fail closed (return an error) if a parsed record does not contain exactly the expected number of fields rather than silently dropping it via filter_map.
